title: fix(plugin-security)!: under a controlled_by_parent declaration whose one master reference is readonly or system, every write that sets it is refused (ADR-0055 §1)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuTXH2TuPG1JBf3xdmP114Fh)_

Fixes #25095

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

⛔ Disclosure ruling `5323310017` (#9387) applies: this PR states the rule and its prescription only. No probe, posture, caller, request or served value is recorded here or in any comment; the measurements are held privately.

> **Route.** Ruling `6345869077` on #25095 chose route B: refuse at the write gate. This PR implements that ruling; it supersedes the narrower insert-only route this draft first carried.

## The rule

ADR-0055 §1 derives a `controlled_by_parent` detail's access from exactly one required `master_detail` that every write of a detail supplies. Since #25092 the parse refuses that master when it is declared `readonly: true` or `system: true` (`controlledByParentMasterRefusal`, shape `master-not-writable`). An object with that declaration still reaches the registry through a door that does not parse:

- a raw `registerObject` or `registerApp`;
- `defineStack(…, { strict: false })`;
- a stored object the boot registers under its `[metadata_spec_invalid]` diagnostic (the registry registers off-spec rows for availability).

On such an object the write gate let writes that set the master reference through, and a detail could end up outside the master its access derives from: readable by nobody, while the write reported success.

**Now** the write gate refuses every write that sets that reference, `422 INVALID_METADATA`, before any master is asked and before anything is written:

- every insert, single or batch, whether or not its body names a master;
- every update whose body carries the reference key as an own property, whatever the value, `null` included (an upsert reaches the gate as one of the two).

The message is the parse's own refusal of the declaration, prefixed with the write it refused, so it carries the parse's prescription: remove the flag and declare the master reference as an ordinary required field, or give the object its own `sharingModel`. Both flags follow one rule, and every caller the gate judges gets the same answer.

**Premise checked first** (ruling item 7): on all three doors above, the object registers, `resolveCbpRelation` resolves its relation, and the flag is readable on the field def the relation came from.

## What changed

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`
  - `CbpRelation.masterNotWritable`: resolved in `resolveCbpRelation` from the same field def the relation came from, judged by `controlledByParentMasterRefusal` on that one def, so the flags and the sentence are spelled once, in the parse. The relation still resolves; the read leg, the cache and `reportCbpMasterUnresolved` are untouched. No second registry reader, and `omissionRefusedByValidation` is not widened.
  - `assertControlledByParentWrite`: right after the missing-relation leg, before any master is asked, `writesMasterReference` (insert always; update when the body carries the key) throws `MasterReferenceNotWritableError`. A delete, and an update that leaves the key alone, take the path they took before.
  - The two stale freeze-note paragraphs at the empty-master branch are rewritten to the current state (both ramp legs have landed, the parse refuses all three shapes, and no insert of theirs reaches that branch). The freeze itself stands.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts`: `MasterReferenceNotWritableError` beside `MasterDetailRelationMissingError` (`INVALID_METADATA`, 422; the error-code ledger already has this row for plugin-security). Not exported. The `MasterReferenceMissingError` docblock is corrected.
- `.changeset/25095-cbp-unwritable-master-write.md`: `patch`, BREAKING, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (already-registered cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired)`, as `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` judges it.
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` and `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`: corrected, because this PR makes them false. They said a write that leaves out a `readonly` or `system` master reference answers `422 MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD`; such a write now answers `422 INVALID_METADATA` (the two-item list above), and the `422 MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` exception is narrowed to a by-id update or delete of a detail whose stored master reference is null. The flat example body moves to that case.

## Unchanged, on purpose

- **Reads.** The relation still resolves, so rows already stored keep the master their reads derive from.
- **A delete, and an update whose body leaves the key out.**
- System contexts (the bypass is unchanged), objects with an ordinary required master, and every object that does not declare `controlled_by_parent`.
- No `packages/spec`, `packages/objectql` or lint change, and no read-side change.
- The served member (`checkControlledByParentWrite`) asks a by-id update with no body, so it never reaches the new refusal, and its closed outcome vocabulary is untouched.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-unwritable-master-write.test.ts` (renamed from `…-insert.test.ts`, 83 cases). Real stack: `ObjectQL` over better-sqlite3, the real `SecurityPlugin`, the real sharing service and middleware, a member context from `resolveAuthzContext` + `assembleExecutionContext`, a platform admin's carried posture, and the engine's security source wired as a kernel wires it, so a detail read composes the engine's `ReadableIds` leaf over its master. The flagged declarations are registered raw through `registerApp`, for `readonly`, `system` and both, on an ordinary object and on a `sys_`-named one. For a member and for a platform admin:

- a single create naming a master, a single create naming none, and a batch create each answer `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 with exactly the parse's message, and nothing is stored; the master walk is never entered;
- a by-id update naming a master, and one setting it to `null`, answer the same, and the row keeps its master;
- controls: a stored row is still read, an update that leaves the key out lands, a delete lands;
- a detail declared as the three in-repo `controlled_by_parent` objects declare theirs (`Field.masterDetail`, `required: true`, through the parse) takes single and batch creates, a re-pointing update, a note update and a delete as before.

A system create lands on every flagged declaration, and each flagged declaration is one the parse refuses at `fields` as `master-not-writable`.

Moved pins, by the ruling: `controlled-by-parent-sharing.test.ts`'s `[#8688]` flagged-insert cases now expect `INVALID_METADATA` with the parse's message (and its stale "AUTHORABLE" wording is corrected); `controlled-by-parent-every-row-master.test.ts`'s cases on its `system`-flagged detail now expect `INVALID_METADATA` for every batch create and every emptying update, and its "the stored master is asked first" ordering pin moves to the validated detail, where it still holds.

Ablation and the gate list are reported in the card's `os-dev-report`.

## Notes

- **Branch.** `claude/project-thread-fi0g2a` is the harness-pinned branch for this session and names no issue, so the Duplicate Fix Guard's branch-name hint will not match. The claim on #25095 (`6345497639`) is the identity record.
- **Serial.** PR #25198 (#24932) landed first; this branch merged `main` after it. The read scope it moved to the engine's `ReadableIds` leaf is not this gate, and the new suite fills the engine's security-source slot the way #25198's rigs do. Split card #25223 waits on this card.
- `packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts` still says a stored `master-not-writable` object "loses the save door" only; a pointer is left for the `domain:spec` seat (#18549), since spec is not this lane's.
- A `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record on the narrowing face is owed before the queue.
